source.title: Geometry matters: insights from Ollivier Ricci Curvature and Ricci Flow into representational alignment through Ollivier-Ricci Curvature and Ricci Flow
source.authors: Nahid Torbati; Michael Gaebler; S. Hofmann; Nico Scherf

record.tranche_reason: The study measures representational alignment using Ollivier–Ricci curvature, Ricci flow, graph distances, and behavioral RDM correlations rather than the original sources’ methods. Its results bear on metric- and input-dependence and on incomplete alignment.
record.gate_note: The study tests human-judgment/network representational alignment for face data, including changes across 2D and 3D viewing conditions and across similarity measures. It does not test model scaling, vision-language alignment, seed convergence, representation mapping, or recurring interpretable features. The reported task-performance scores are context for the alignment results, not separate alignment rows. Values in figures without extractable numerical results are not recorded as numerical rows.
record.test_reason: This study does not test any version. It measures alignment between human face-similarity judgments and a VGG-Face variant fine-tuned to predict those judgments, so the alignment is induced on purpose. The only model-to-model comparison is Aligned-VGG against VGG-Face, and Aligned-VGG shares VGG-Face's frozen layers up to FC7, so the two are not independently trained. There is no scale sweep, no cross-modal pairing, no seed comparison, no mapping test and no feature-universality test. The metric-dependence finding (Euclidean/cosine versus flow-metric RSA) concerns human–network alignment, a related but different construct from convergence between independently trained models. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis appears only in related work.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct, with two precisions. In the 3D condition the network is trained on judgments from the dynamic 3D viewing condition, and it notably fails to form the female-face cluster. The authors also conclude that successful alignment requires the model's capacities to match the complexity of human experience.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Ollivier–Ricci curvature, discrete Ricci flow, graph-distance comparisons, and human behavioral judgments; it does not test the original sources’ model-scale, cross-modal, or seed-convergence procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment conclusions vary with viewing condition and similarity measure. The paper also reports that increasing graph connectivity modestly improves only the Aligned-VGG versus VGG-Face alignment score while Human Judgment remains separate.

fits_no_version.finding: Human vs Aligned-VGG RSA in 3D gives r=0.54 (Euclidean) and r=0.43 (cosine) but drops to r=0.33 with the flow-metric. Curvature distances show the 3D-trained network stays closer to baseline VGG-Face than to humans.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Measured human–network representational alignment depends on the similarity metric; geometry-aware metrics reveal misalignment that Euclidean or cosine RSA miss.

fits_no_version.finding: A network trained on human odd-one-out judgments reaches human-like geometry and community structure with 2D-condition data. With 3D-condition data it does not, despite similar task performance (0.72 vs 0.69).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Behavioural alignment of a network to human judgments does not guarantee alignment of representational geometry under a modality mismatch.

record.problems: The study examines one model family and controlled, computer-generated faces; the authors identify generalization to other architectures and more naturalistic images as future work. The graph analysis depends on discrete curvature approximations. Several figure-based analyses have no numerical values stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Numerical values not stated in the text for Figures 4-14 are not transcribed.

untested.parts: All: no scale sweep and no independently trained models with different architectures or data.
All: no mapping, stitching or relative-representation test.
Metric dependence is shown only for human-vs-trained-network RSA, not for convergence between independent models.
No measure of convergence between independent models, plateau or cause.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked every row to V6/V7 and labelled both as supported. I reject this: the study concerns human–model alignment induced by training, and its only model–model pair shares frozen weights. It is not evidence about convergence among independently trained models, so all rows are set to none and no verdicts are given. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis is cited only in related work.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep, and no comparison of independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data.
The study compares human judgments and a face network across 2D and dynamic 3D viewing conditions; it does not compare vision and language models on paired images and captions.
No comparison across initialization seeds or analysis of shared features or subspaces.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired representation-transfer test.
No test of recurring neurons, SAE features, or circuits across models.
The study varies distance/similarity measures and viewing condition, but does not test other datasets, out-of-distribution inputs, or nearest-neighbor settings as a general account of convergence.

It reports incomplete behavioral-to-network geometric alignment in a modality-mismatch setting, but does not test scaling, plateaus across scale, or whether shared training data/objectives explain alignment.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: 2D versus 3D viewing and compared RDM/graph measures
reader_labels.reason: The apparent alignment changes with the metric and viewing condition: the 3D RDM correlations differ across Euclidean, cosine, and flow metrics, and the geometric distances and curvature profiles show weaker human/network correspondence in 3D (R1-R24).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Aligned-VGG compared with human judgments in 2D and 3D face-viewing conditions
reader_labels.reason: The network is reported to match human geometry and community structure in 2D, but only partially in 3D, where its curvature and community structure are closer to baseline VGG-Face and it fails to recover the human organization (R1, R5-R6, R11-R12, R17-R20, R25, R30, R35, R40-R44).
